title: Deep linear networks: learning dynamics through the SVD
summary: Factorised linear maps, rank/SVD assumptions, solvable balanced-mode dynamics, Euler experiments and careful representation similarity.

objectives.description: Derive factorised linear-network gradients and rank constraints.
Use SVD with explicit whitening/alignment assumptions rather than asserting automatic decoupling.
Solve and numerically test a balanced-mode gradient-flow model.
Distinguish dot-product and cosine similarity and test representation claims under coordinate changes.

preparation.description: Read deep linear networks, SVD, representation similarity and transient correlations; use the lesson to qualify alignment and cosine conventions.

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A linear network has a convex objective in all its layer parameters.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Its product is linear in inputs, but factorisation makes the parameter objective generally nonconvex.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A Gram matrix is always a cosine-similarity matrix.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Cosine requires row-norm normalisation; raw dot products depend on magnitude.

commonMisconceptions.claim: SVD proves that every network learns independent modes.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The solvable mode analysis requires specific input covariance, alignment and loss assumptions.
